name: MA-03
label: Safe D

key_factors: Trahan holds a roughly 200-to-1 cash advantage ($1.8M vs. $6.6K) over her Republican opponent
District leans Democratic by about 11 points and sits in deeply blue Massachusetts
Prediction markets price a Democratic win near 96%
No public general-election polls or expert ratings are available
model.rationale: Trahan combines incumbency, a D+11 district, and an overwhelming financial edge against a challenger who has raised under $9,000, while markets price her win probability at about 96%. With no contrary polling or ratings, the fundamentals alone support a Safe Democratic rating.
model.watch: Any late infusion of outside spending for Grossi or an unforeseen controversy around Trahan would be the main way this race narrows.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Lori Trahan, the Democratic incumbent, is seeking re-election in a Massachusetts district that has leaned about 11 points Democratic in recent federal races. Her Republican opponent, Gary Grossi, has raised roughly $8,000, while Trahan has built about $1.8 million in cash on hand. An independent candidate, Dennis Conlon, is also on the ballot with no visible campaign activity.

No public general-election polls or expert ratings cover this race, so the picture rests on fundamentals and markets. Prediction markets give the Democratic side roughly a 96 percent chance of holding the seat. The combination of incumbency, the district's partisan lean, and a lopsided fundraising gap makes an upset highly improbable. The contest is rated Safe Democratic, with turnout in a low-salience election the main open question.
